stem:
A 29-year-old patient with migraine preceded by visual aura wants reliable contraception for several years and would prefer lighter periods. She has heavy regular bleeding, with a normal examination and no identified uterine cavity abnormality. Pregnancy and infection are excluded, and there is no contraindication to intrauterine contraception.

Which option best meets her goals?

options.label: A
options.text: A combined oral contraceptive pill taken continuously to reduce bleeding
options.explanation: Migraine with aura contraindicates any combined oestrogen method because of ischaemic stroke risk, however it is taken.

options.label: B
options.text: A copper intrauterine device, which contains no hormone
options.explanation: A copper IUD suits aura but typically makes periods heavier, working against her second goal.

options.label: C
options.text: An etonogestrel implant, which avoids oestrogen and lasts three years
options.explanation: The implant is safe with aura and long-acting, but its bleeding pattern is unpredictable and it does not treat heavy menstrual bleeding.

options.label: D
options.text: A 52 mg levonorgestrel intrauterine device for several years
options.explanation: A 52 mg LNG-IUD is safe with aura, provides long-acting contraception and markedly reduces heavy menstrual bleeding.

options.label: E
options.text: A combined vaginal ring, as it gives lower systemic oestrogen exposure
options.explanation: The ring is still a combined oestrogen method and is contraindicated with migraine with aura.

context: An LNG-IUD can meet contraception and heavy-bleeding goals in a patient with migraine with aura.
